messages:
incident-bot: 🔴 HIGH — Multiple nodes in infer-gpu-pool-usw reporting NotReady and kubelet restarts. 25% of pool unavailable. Paging on-call.

alice: Ack. I'm oncall. seeing alerts in console. starting triage.

ben: pulling logs, opening k9s. which nodes are affected?

priya: FYI runtime alerts show several llm-runtime containers restarting with OOMKilled and a handful of CUDA errors in kernel logs. Might be correlated with kubelet restarts.

marco: Confirmed from node-monitor: node-az2-a (ip 10.2.3.45) and node-az2-b (10.2.3.46) flipped NotReady around 5422223290. Kernel dmesg on node-az2-a shows GPU driver reset.

alice: Paste kubectl output:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep infer-gpu-pool-usw
node-az2-a   NotReady   2d    v1.26.5   10.2.3.45   <none>   gpu=true
node-az2-b   NotReady   3m    v1.26.5   10.2.3.46   <none>   gpu=true
node-az2-c   Ready      5d    v1.26.5   10.2.3.47   <none>   gpu=true
```

ben: Also seeing multiple pods in CrashLoopBackOff on those nodes: llm-runtime v2.3.1 containers OOMKilled. sample: `kubectl describe pod llm-runtime-abc -n inference` shows repeated "oom_kill".

priya: Runtime stacktrace snippet from pod: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. attempted 11.2GB, free 1.1GB
  at /app/serve/generate.py:312
  ...
```
That lines up with driver resets causing GPU memory accounting to get weird.

marco: Node dmesg (redacted): 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12345.679000] kernel: watchdog: task kubelet blocked for more than 120 seconds.
[ 12346.000000] systemd: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
```

alice: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon the two affected nodes, 2) drain low-priority pods, 3) scale up infer-gpu-pool-usw autoscaler by +2 nodes, 4) enable fallback routing to cpu-backed model variant for non-SLA traffic. applying now.

alice: `kubectl cordon node-az2-a && kubectl drain node-az2-a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

ben: Doing same for node-az2-b. Starting drains. Will mark affected customer-facing routes as degraded in console so SREs and CS know.

priya: In parallel, I'm starting an emergency rollout of llm-runtime 2.3.2-hotpatch (contains extra memory guardrails + retry backoff). Command: `kubectl set image ds/llm-runtime llm-runtime=redwood/llm-runtime:2.3.2-hotpatch -n inference`

marco: I'm reprovisioning two replacement nodes in the pool (usw-spot-alloc). autoscaler request submitted, ETA ~3m. Also kicking off node-driver restart on other nodes to preemptively clear stale driver state: `systemctl restart nvidia-driver` via kexec job.

alice: Traffic steering: switching routing weight so ~80% traffic goes to other regions (us-east-1) and 20% to usw for degraded requests. doing now.

sre-bot: Route update applied: infer-routing/usw -> weight 0.2, failover -> use infer-gpu-pool-useast primary.

ben: Customer impact: from metrics window (last 10m) ~4.2k requests failed with 5xx, 6 customers reported latency spikes. Majority are experimental/low-priority eval jobs. tagging alerts and notifying CS to inform impacted accounts.

priya: Observability note: the hotpatch reduces per-request GPU allocation by 10% and adds aggressive batch-splitting; should reduce OOM pressure while we stabilize.

alice: Handing to ben for monitoring and follow-up once drains complete. I'll stay on for 15m then hand to night oncall if still open.

ben: Ack — I'll monitor logs and metrics, validate hotpatch rollout, and patch any remaining CrashLoopBackOffs. If nodes remain unstable after replacements, we'll open a vendor ticket with GPU infra.

marco: Replacement nodes are Ready (5422223560). starting pod reschedules.

ben: Hotpatch rollout shows 60% pods updated, success probes passing on most. Few pods still failing on old nodes but draining finishes and re-schedules to new nodes.

alice: Quick customer note to CS channel: "We observed a regional GPU node instability causing transient inference failures in us-west-2. We’ve cordoned affected hosts, rolled a runtime hotpatch, reprovisioned nodes, and steered most traffic to another region. Engineers continue to monitor; degraded mode remains for low-priority traffic." :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident severity reduced to MEDIUM. Autoscaler added 2 nodes.

ben: All pods on replaced nodes now stable, no further OOM traces after hotpatch. GPU driver logs on replaced nodes look clean.

priya: I'll follow up with an eval job to run a stress suite overnight to validate memory accounting under the hotpatch.

marco: I'll open a support case with GPU vendor about the Xid 79 resets and attach node logs.

alice: Closing on-call for now — handing to ben for overnight watch. If anything flares escalate to Priya.

ben: Taking over. Last check: latency back to baseline for SLA routes, error rate down to normal. setting alert thresholds slightly tighter for next 24h.

alice: Thanks team. Filing short post-incident note and root-cause next steps in #incidents.

sre-bot: Incident thread closed (temporary).
